title: The 61% rule: what actually goes viral

pages.headline: 61% of viral posts do one boring thing
pages.deck: A study of 438,413 posts found the pattern is not the hook everyone copies.

pages.label: Share of top-1% posts that use it
pages.body: Quantified proof: a real number, from a named source, in the first two lines. Not an adjective. Not a promise.

pages.headline: A number beats a question
pages.body: Opening with a precise number lifts median likes 17%. Opening with a question drops them 28%. Same idea, different first line.

pages.headline: Say who, when, how much
pages.body: Posts high on specificity beat their own baseline 68% of the time. Vague ones land at 50% — a coin flip.

pages.headline: The line that decides it
pages.left: AI is changing how teams work. Here are my thoughts.
pages.right: We cut 9 hours a week off one report. The tool cost nothing.

pages.quote: Specificity is the moat: a date, a number, a detail only you could know.
pages.body: It is also the one thing a model cannot invent for you.

pages.headline: Imperative hooks are dead
pages.body: "Stop doing this" scores 0.02× on engagement lift. It reads as a command from a stranger, and the feed treats it that way.

pages.label: Do this today
pages.headline: Rewrite one first line
pages.body: Take your last post. Replace the opening question with the most specific number you can defend. Keep everything else.

pages.headline: One idea, decoded, every week
pages.body: Plain English, a real source, and one thing to do with it.
